issues.description: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame.service typed as live FrameProcessor leaks implementation through the frame contract
issues.detail: Embedding a stateful FrameProcessor reference in a control-frame dataclass is the wrong shape. It couples the frame's ADT to the full processor abstraction, exposes mutable state to downstream observers, makes the frame unserializable, and forces identity-based equality. Carry a stable identifier (service id/name) and resolve at the switcher.

issues.description: Suppression key uses fragile equality on FrameProcessor instances
issues.detail: `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` falls back to identity unless overridden. If active_service is wrapped, proxied, or re-instantiated, the invariant 'request to active service is consumed' breaks silently and the frame leaks downstream. Use `is` explicitly or compare a stable identifier so the invariant is testable.

issues.description: Handler contract for who consumes/re-pushes the frame is unstated and split across components
issues.detail: Previously the switcher consumed the request frame unconditionally; now STTService re-pushes it and the switcher only suppresses when service == active_service. Outside a switcher the frame escapes downstream, and STTService subclasses overriding process_frame silently violate the new postcondition. Document the contract on the frame and STTService, or centralize re-push.

issues.description: Rename is a breaking public-API change with no deprecation alias
issues.detail: RequestMetadataFrame was an exported symbol. Renaming it outright breaks downstream users on the next version bump. A one-line `RequestMetadataFrame = ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame` alias with a DeprecationWarning costs nothing and preserves back-compat.

issues.description: Forward-reference string annotation hides a missing import
issues.detail: The dataclass field is annotated as the string "FrameProcessor". This only works because dataclasses don't resolve annotations at runtime; any `get_type_hints` call or schema introspection will fail. Either import FrameProcessor properly or stop pretending the field is typed.

issues.description: Switcher-internal frame lives in the global frames module
issues.detail: The frame is explicitly switcher-internal per its docstring and prefix, yet it sits in pipecat.frames.frames alongside public frames. Co-locating it with service_switcher (or a switcher frames submodule) would draw the module boundary around responsibility and signal to callers that this is not a general-purpose control frame.

synthesis.summary: The rename clarifies intent and the diff is small and readable, but the panel agrees the new frame shape is wrong: a live FrameProcessor reference is embedded in a control-frame dataclass and the switcher relies on instance equality to decide suppression. The handler contract — who consumes the frame, who re-pushes it, what happens outside a ServiceSwitcher — is split across components without being written down, creating an LSP hazard for STTService subclasses. Secondary concerns: no deprecation alias for the public rename, a forward-reference annotation that hides a missing import, and switcher-internal types living in the global frames module. NEEDS-WORK: narrow `service` to a stable identifier, document the handler contract, and add a back-compat alias before landing.
